Problem numbers refer to the textbook (Chiang & Wainwright, 4th edition). These are not graded, but you should attempt them all before the quiz. Try each question yourself first, then expand the **Solution** to check.

## Exercise 10.5

**1.** Find the derivatives of:

a. $y=e^{2t+4}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=2e^{2t+4}$$

</details>

b. $y=e^{1-9t}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=-9e^{1-9t}$$

</details>

c. $y=e^{t^{2}+1}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=2te^{t^{2}+1}$$

</details>

d. $y=5e^{2-t^{2}}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=-10te^{2-t^{2}}$$

</details>

e. $y=e^{ax^{2}+bx+c}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=(2ax+b)e^{ax^{2}+bx+c}$$

</details>

f. $y=xe^{x}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=x\frac{d}{dx}e^{x}+e^{x}\frac{d}{dx}x=xe^{x}+e^{x}=(x+1)e^{x}$$

</details>

g. $y=x^{2}e^{2x}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{2}\left(2e^{2x}\right)+2xe^{2x}=2x(x+1)e^{2x}$$

</details>

h. $y=axe^{bx+c}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=a\left(xbe^{bx+c}+e^{bx+c}\right)=a(bx+1)e^{bx+c}$$

</details>

**3.** Find the derivatives of:

a. $y=\ln\left(7t^{5}\right)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{35t^{4}}{7t^{5}}=\frac{5}{t}$$

</details>

b. $y=\ln\left(at^{10}\right)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{10at^{9}}{at^{10}}=\frac{10}{t}$$

</details>

c. $y=\ln(t+19)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{1}{t+19}$$

</details>

d. $y=5\ln(t+1)^{2}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dt}=5\cdot\frac{2(t+1)}{(t+1)^{2}}=\frac{10}{t+1}$$

</details>

e. $y=\ln x-\ln(1+x)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{1+x}=\frac{1}{x(1+x)}$$

</details>

f. $y=\ln\left[x(1-x)^{8}\right]$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\ln x+8\ln(1-x)\right]=\frac{1}{x}-\frac{8}{1-x}=\frac{1-9x}{x(1-x)}$$

</details>

g. $y=\ln\left(\frac{2x}{1+x}\right)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\ln 2x-\ln(1+x)\right]=\frac{2}{2x}-\frac{1}{1+x}=\frac{1}{x(1+x)}$$

</details>

h. $y=5x^{4}\ln x^{2}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dy}{dx} &= 5x^{4}\cdot\frac{2x}{x^{2}}+20x^{3}\ln x^{2} \\
&= 10x^{3}\left(1+2\ln x^{2}\right)=10x^{3}(1+4\ln x)
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

**7.** Find the derivatives of the following by first taking the natural log of both sides:

a. $y=\dfrac{3x}{(x+2)(x+4)}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Since $\ln y=\ln 3x-\ln(x+2)-\ln(x+4)$,

$$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{x+2}-\frac{1}{x+4}=\frac{8-x^{2}}{x(x+2)(x+4)}$$

Hence,

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dy}{dx} &= \frac{8-x^{2}}{x(x+2)(x+4)}\cdot\frac{3x}{(x+2)(x+4)} \\
&= \frac{3\left(8-x^{2}\right)}{(x+2)^{2}(x+4)^{2}}
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

b. $y=\left(x^{2}+3\right)e^{x^{2}+1}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Since $\ln y=\ln\left(x^{2}+3\right)+x^{2}+1$,

$$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2x}{x^{2}+3}+2x=\frac{2x\left(x^{2}+4\right)}{x^{2}+3}$$

Hence,

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2x\left(x^{2}+4\right)}{x^{2}+3}\cdot\left(x^{2}+3\right)e^{x^{2}+1}=2x\left(x^{2}+4\right)e^{x^{2}+1}$$

</details>
